listing.name: C-Dogs SDL
listing.summary: Play C-Dogs through your Linux distribution or a permitted existing desktop copy.

steps.title: Install from your Linux distribution
steps.instruction: On Debian or Ubuntu, use your package manager to install cdogs-sdl. It brings in the matching C-Dogs data package and SDL libraries. Debian provides x86-64 and ARM64 packages. Start C-Dogs SDL normally from your applications menu or run cdogs-sdl. Your distribution handles software updates.

steps.title: Use a permitted Flatpak copy
steps.instruction: Flathub provides C-Dogs SDL for x86-64 and ARM64 as io.github.cxong.cdogs-sdl. Open it from your application menu. Flatpak owns its updates. The package includes the Wolfenstein 3D shareware files.

steps.title: Use an existing copy you have permission to play
steps.instruction: Keep the full copy, including bin, graphics, data, missions and libraries. On Windows, the publisher ZIP uses the 32-bit bin/cdogs-sdl.exe player. On Linux x86-64, the publisher tarball needs glibc 2.34 or later, SDL2 and SDL2_mixer. Open a terminal in bin and run ./cdogs-sdl so it finds the data in the parent directory.

steps.title: Register your existing Windows player
steps.instruction: In Portcove, choose bin/cdogs-sdl.exe from your permitted Windows copy and choose its bin folder as the working directory. Review the selected player and folder, then choose Play. Keep backups of the complete package and your actual C-Dogs profile. Removing this registration keeps those external files; you and upstream still own updates and backups.

warnings: The publisher Windows, Linux and Mac packages bundle Wolfenstein 3D shareware. The Debian-derived data package excludes that bundle. Use only originals and additional campaigns that you have permission to use.

references.title: Resume a backed-up campaign
references.instruction: With C-Dogs SDL closed, restore autosave.json to the profile folder for the copy you use. Leave the saved campaign available in the game. Open Start, choose Continue, and after selecting your players choose Continue with the saved mission number. Start campaign begins from the first mission.

references.title: Use a permitted Apple Silicon copy
references.instruction: The publisher disk image contains an Apple Silicon player targeting macOS 11 or later. Keep the complete cdogs-sdl folder and its SDL frameworks together. The executable is bin/cdogs-sdl. Intel Macs need a separately prepared source build.

references.title: Register an existing Linux portable copy
references.instruction: Use absolute paths to bin/cdogs-sdl and its bin folder. For c-dogs-sdl, run external select-preview with the executable path and --working-directory for the folder. Repeat both paths with external select and pass the preview SHA-256 to --expected-preview. Start the game with portcove exec c-dogs-sdl.

references.title: Keep your settings, campaigns and progress
references.instruction: Keep autosave.json, options.cnf and your custom campaigns. The standard Windows ZIP uses C-Dogs SDL under %APPDATA%. The Linux and Mac archives normally use ~/.config/cdogs-sdl. Flatpak uses ~/.var/app/io.github.cxong.cdogs-sdl/config/cdogs-sdl. If you set XDG_CONFIG_HOME, use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cdogs-sdl. For other profile redirects, keep the actual folder you use.

listing.download_block_reason: Portcove downloads are held for the bundled Wolfenstein 3D shareware data. Debian-derived packages supply the C-Dogs campaigns without that bundle.
